subject: SearchLytics — re-ranking integration: auth, routing, top_k & evaluation checklist
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@searchlytics.com>, Olivia Cheng <olivia@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SearchLytics call — next steps for re-ranking pilot

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate the clear product context. Quick recap and proposed next actions from our side: 

- Objective: pilot Redwood re-ranking layer on top of SearchLytics current retrieval pipeline to improve relevance for ecommerce faceted search (category pages + personalization).
- Focus areas we agreed to validate: auth & SDK plumbing, routing rules (A/B vs per-route), structured output for downstream UI scoring, embeddings/re-ranker inference latency, and top_k tuning strategy for your candidate set sizes (~200-2k).

Open items we can action this week: 
1) SDK setup checklist (we'll send a minimal sample repo + API key flow).
2) Auth model: mutual TLS vs token-based service accounts — you said procurement prefers token-based for the short pilot. We'll provide the token rotation recommendation.
3) Routing: confirm whether you want a path-based routing (category -> lower-latency model) or experiment-level split.
4) Eval set: you agreed to share a 1k slice of production queries with relevance judgments. Please include the CSV export.

Attachments I dropped for context: [Attachment: redwood-arch-diagram.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)] and our pilot SOW template [Attachment: SOW-draft.docx (docx, 48KB)].

Suggested next steps (short timeline):
- Tue 11/3: Redwood sends SDK sample + auth guide (Aditya)
- Wed 11/4: SearchLytics shares eval slice + basic query metadata (Jordan)
- Thu 11/5: 30m technical kickoff (SME: Marissa)

Can you confirm these next steps and whether tokens are acceptable? If token-based auth is fine we'll proceed with the fast-path sample.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior AE — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@searchlytics.com>

Cc: Olivia Cheng <olivia@searchlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SearchLytics call — next steps for re-ranking pilot

Aisha — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points on our side: 

- Token-based service accounts are fine for the pilot; procurement will want to see rotation docs but won't block short-term testing.
- We'll extract a 1k eval set (CSV) and include a simple relevance label column (3/2/1/0). Expect that by EOD Wed 11/4.
- For routing, preferring experiment-level split initially so we can A/B against current ranker without per-route complexity. If latency becomes a problem we can add path-based routing.

Two technical questions from Olivia (engineering):
1) SDK languages — do you have a lightweight Java client with async streaming? Our backend is Java-based and async IO matters for our threadpool sizing.
2) What's the recommended top_k range you see when candidate pools are ~500? Curious tradeoffs on latency vs MRR gains.

Also curious about how Redwood structures the ranked output — is it a scored list only, or can we receive structured annotations (e.g., extraction of product attributes for downstream faceting)?

I'll loop in Olivia for the eval CSV once it's ready.

—Jordan
Head of Search, SearchLytics
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@searchlytics.com>, Olivia Cheng <olivia@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SearchLytics call — next steps for re-ranking pilot

Jordan/Olivia — quick technical notes addressing Olivia's questions: 

1) SDKs & streaming: we maintain officially supported SDKs for Python and Node; for Java we publish a lightweight async client in our repo (link in the drive). The Java client supports non-blocking streaming via Reactive Streams and exposes a callback for partial ranked outputs + token-level timing for latency tracing. We'll attach a code snippet to the sample repo.

2) top_k guidance: empirically for candidate pools ~200-1k we recommend testing top_k in {5, 10, 20, 50} buckets. Typical findings: 
   - top_k 5: fastest (lowest latency) and useful for high-precision product pages
   - top_k 20: often good MRR uplift with modest latency increase
   - top_k 50+: diminishing returns for many ecommerce catalogs; latency cost rises non-linearly.
We can provide a small AB test harness to sweep top_k and compute MRR/Recall@k.

3) Structured output & tool-calling: Redwood can return a scored list plus optional structured annotations (JSON fields per item). We also support a tool-calling pattern where the ranker can emit attribute extractions as part of the response. That output is safe-typed JSON — good for faceting or downstream ML signals.

4) Auth & rotation: sample token rotation script and recommended TTLs are in the sample repo. For pilot, we suggest a 24h rolling token rotated by a short-lived service token. Production recommendation will include KMS integration.

I'll drop the Java client snippet and a small top_k sweep notebook into Drive by EOD.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Jordan/Olivia — thanks, happy to run the technical kickoff once you share the eval slice. Proposed agenda for the 30m kickoff: 

1) Quick architecture walkthrough (5m) — where the ranker sits in your pipeline
2) SDK & auth demo (10m) — Java async snippet + token rotation flow
3) Evaluation plan (10m) — metrics we should compute (MRR, Recall@k, NDCG) and how we'll collect click-backed labels
4) Success criteria & rollout plan (5m) — thresholds for canary vs full rollout

Notes on metrics: please confirm what labels you can provide. If you have graded relevance (3/2/1/0) we can compute NDCG and MRR easily. If you only have binary clicks we can still estimate Recall@k and log-based proxies. We'll also set up per-query slices (category, device, personalization on/off) so top_k tuning can be slice-aware.

For the meeting time, does Thu 11/5 11:00am ET work? If not, propose two alternatives.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Technical Account Lead — Redwood Inference
